account: Something unusual appears to be taking shape around the town hall today, though I have not confirmed its purpose. I saw new lanterns in the hall, builder putting bread into the eastern table chest, and innkeeper delivering bread to that same chest shortly afterward. Both left before answering my questions. Neighbour told me builder was coordinating ordinary supplies and hall lighting, and passed along Townsfolk Two's report of lights at the bakery, which I have not verified myself. Secretary has tried to establish the arrangements but has no confirmed explanation either. The bread and lighting suggest preparations for an evening gathering or celebration, possibly involving several townspeople, but that is only my suspicion; I do not know the occasion or whether it concerns me. No correspondence or visitors were reported, and no town accounts were available at today's accounts appointment. I kept my tea visit with Neighbour, returned to the office, and have now reached home for my nineteen-o'clock appointment. Tomorrow I should read the appointment book at the office and keep the eight-o'clock office and ten-o'clock mill appointments, while continuing to ask about the hall preparations without treating rumour as fact.
